tool.name: tls_audit
tool.description:
Audit TLS / SSL configuration on a target host — emits findings for weak protocols, weak ciphers, and certificate problems.
Standard pentest deliverable; clients always expect a TLS section. Implementation uses Python's `ssl` module + `cryptography` for certificate parsing rather than shelling out to `openssl s_client` — cleaner, no subprocess overhead, full Python error handling.
Probes (one connection each, all bounded by `timeout`):
| Test | Trigger | Severity | |---|---|---| | TLS 1.0 / 1.1 acceptance | Server completes handshake at that version | medium (CWE-326) | | TLS 1.2 / 1.3 acceptance | (Informational — confirms modern support) | info | | NULL / aNULL ciphers | Cipher cohort accepted | high (CWE-327) | | EXPORT-grade ciphers | Cipher cohort accepted | high (CWE-327) | | RC4 | Cipher cohort accepted | high (CWE-327) | | 3DES (Sweet32) | Cipher cohort accepted | high (CWE-327) | | Single-DES | Cipher cohort accepted | high (CWE-327) | | Certificate expired | `now > notAfter` | high (CWE-298) | | Certificate expiring soon | within 30 days | low (CWE-298) | | Self-signed certificate | issuer == subject | medium (CWE-295) | | Hostname mismatch | host doesn't match CN or SANs | high (CWE-297) |
Each finding includes `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (the §11 non-tech UX fields) so the wrapper renders dashboard cards with concrete fix instructions per issue (nginx / Apache / Let's Encrypt / certbot config snippets).
Side-effect output: certificate SANs are returned in `result.certificate.sans` — feed these back into `subdomain_enum` or the surface map for additional subdomain discovery.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to each connection. Exclude-path isn't path-relative for TLS audit (the audit is on host:port, not a URL path) so that flag is a no-op for this tool.

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: Hostname / hostname:port / URL. Default port 443. Examples: `example.com`, `example.com:8443`, `https://example.com/`. Path component (if any) is dropped — TLS audit is host:port-scoped.

returns.description:
{success, target, host, port, protocols: {"TLS 1.0": {accepted, error}, ...}, weak_ciphers: {"RC4": {accepted, negotiated_cipher, ...}, ...}, certificate: {present, subject_cn, issuer_cn, sans, expired, days_until_expiry, self_signed, hostname_match, ...}, findings_emitted}.
`certificate.sans` is a list of DNS names from the cert's Subject Alternative Names extension — the agent should feed this list into `subdomain_enum` to extend the discovered surface.
